learningGoals: Learn to add 's' to everyday naming words to show there is more than one (e.g., cat to cats). 🐱🐱
Learn to add 'es' to special words that end in s, x, sh, or ch (e.g., box to boxes). 📦📦
Confidently count objects around them and use the correct 'one' or 'many' word. 🎈
keyVocabulary: Naming Words (Names of people, places, animals, or things) 🏷️
Add 's' (The magic letter we add to make words mean many) ➕s
Add 'es' (The special letters for words ending in x, s, ch, sh) ➕es
More than one (Having two, three, or a hundred!) 💯
teachingTips: Laundry Time Math: While folding clothes, ask your child to help. Say, 'Here is one shirt. Oh look, now we have two shirts! Can you hear the S?' 👕👚
Snack Time Plurals: Count snacks together. 'You have one almond, but I have three almonds! Let us add an S.' 🥜
The 'ES' Hunt: Look for household items like a box, brush, or glass. Say, 'One glass, but we need many glasses for the family! We add an ES sound here.' 🥛🥛
Storybook Detective: While reading a bedtime story, point to pictures and ask, 'Is there one bird or many birds here?' Let them read the 's' at the end of the word. 📖🐦

funActivities.title: The 'S' Magic Wand 🪄
funActivities.description: Give your child a pretend magic wand (like a pencil or stick). Point to one object (like a toy) and say 'Toy'. When they tap a pile of toys, they have to shout the magic word with an 's' (Toys!) to make the plural magic work. 🧸

funActivities.title: One and Many Basket Sort 🧺
funActivities.description: Set up two baskets labeled 'One' and 'Many'. Hand your child real objects (1 pen, 3 crayons, 1 book, 5 blocks) and have them sort them into the correct basket while saying the words out loud, emphasizing the 's' or 'es' sound. 🖍️

funActivities.title: Playdough Plurals 🔴
funActivities.description: Use playdough to make simple shapes. Make one apple, then make three apples. Practice saying 'Apple' for one, and then stretching out the 's' sound like a snake for 'Applessss' when pointing to the many pile! 🐍🍎
